title: Graceful exit plan for legacy JSON-RPC endpoints and model-tag cleanup
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket defines the product plan to deprecate the legacy JSON-RPC transport endpoints (v0/jsonrpc/*) and to prune outdated model tags/aliases that were historically used for back-compat. The goal is to minimize client disruption while reclaiming routing complexity and reducing maintenance burden on the routing and model-onboarding teams.
background: We currently support two parallel transports: modern REST/streaming unified generate endpoints and an older JSON-RPC surface introduced in the early platform. JSON-RPC traffic has declined to <2% of total requests, but it increases complexity in proxying, telemetry, and model alias compatibility. Several model aliases (eg. 'redwood-chat-legacy', 'rwd-gen-v0-compat') are no longer produced by model infra and cause confusing fallbacks. This plan lays out a phased deprecation, client migration guidance, telemetry gates, and rollback criteria.
scope: In scope: public announcement and documentation updates, SDK patches, server-side deprecation headers, automatic alias-to-new-model redirects for 90 days, telemetry/alerting, migration CLI for large customers. Out of scope: forcing immediate client-side rewrites, on-prem appliance upgrades (handled in Private deployment roadmap).
scope_changes: Initial scope included a forced 30-day cutoff for alias redirects. After engineering review (ENG-83477), scope changed to a 90-day redirect window with a second 90-day removal buffer for enterprise customers on Dedicated plans. This change increases migration effort but reduces customer downtime risk.
acceptance_criteria:
1) SDKs (python/js/go) log a deprecation warning and surface automated mapping helpers.
2) Server responds to JSON-RPC v0 requests with Deprecation header + migration URL and a stable 307 redirect for supported models during 90-day window.
3) Telemetry shows decreasing JSON-RPC traffic trend (target: -70% in first 60 days).
4) No regression on latency P50/P95 for unified endpoints after alias pruning (<= +5% allowed).
5) Completed communications sent to top 50 customers using legacy endpoints with tailored migration artifacts.
6) Rollback plan documented and validated via tabletop exercise with SRE and Support.
migration_timeline:
Phase 0 (Mar 2026): Finalize spec, security review, SDK PRs opened.
Phase 1 (Apr 2026 - 90 days): Soft deprecation: return Deprecation headers + in-band migration guidance, 307 redirect for mapped aliases, SDKs include helper methods and warnings.
Phase 2 (Jul 2026 - 90 days): Announced pruning window begins for non-enterprise customers; redirects become informational (no automatic mapping) while enterprise customers get extended support.
Phase 3 (Oct 2026): Model-tag/prune job runs to remove obsolete aliases; JSON-RPC endpoints return 410 for pruned routes.
Phase 4 (Nov 2026): Final telemetry review and close ticket or extend remediation for customers flagged by migration tooling.
rollout_plan:
- Week 0: Public blog post + changelog entry describing timeline and helpful links.
- Week 1: SDK patch release (python/js/go) with migration helper and deprecation log.
- Week 4: Enable Deprecation header and pilot redirects for a small set of low-traffic aliases.
- Week 6: Broad redirect rollout for all remaining aliases for 90 days.
- Week 20: Begin pruning window for customers not on Dedicated/Private plans.
- Ongoing: Support & Solutions Engineering outreach to top customers, automatic migration CLI offered as opt-in.
telemetry_and_gates:
Telemetry: count of JSON-RPC requests per model alias, 7/14/30-day rolling trends, SDK migration adoption rate, and error rates for redirected requests.
Gates: do not progress to pruning if: (a) top-10 active customers still have >50% traffic on JSON-RPC, OR (b) redirected request error rate increases >3x baseline for >24h.
Alerting: Pager duty if redirect error spike or unexpected latency increase on unified endpoints.
client_guidance:
Raw HTTP clients: Update base path from /v0/jsonrpc/* to /v1/generate or /v1/chat/completions; map JSON-RPC params to unified request body using provided mapping table (see linked artifact).
SDK users: Upgrade to next minor version which auto-detects JSON-RPC calls and prints migration steps. Use SDK.migrate_jsonrpc_to_unified(helper) for batch migrations.
Enterprise: We will provide a migration-runner CLI that can rewrite recorded request logs to the new contract and a dry-run mode for validation.
Fallback strategy: If immediate rewrite not possible, configure client to hit the redirecting gateway which will return guidance and a temporarily mapped backend for 90 days.
compatibility_matrix:
Legacy JSON-RPC method -> Unified endpoint mapping examples:
- jsonrpc.createChat -> /v1/chat/completions (map 'messages' field, preserve 'conversation_id' as metadata)
- jsonrpc.generateText -> /v1/generate (map 'prompt' and 'max_tokens')
- jsonrpc.embed -> /v1/embeddings (map 'model' and 'input' arrays)
Note: some older parameters (e.g., 'streamingMode': 'longpoll') will be deprecated without direct mapping and require client-side changes.
api_contract_changes:
New behavior: servers will include HTTP header 'Deprecation: true; removal-date=2026-10-01' during Phase 1. Redirect behavior: temporary 307 with 'Location' pointing to migration docs and suggested endpoint. Error codes: legacy 400 -> new 422 for param shape mismatch.
We will publish a table of exact header values and error-code mappings in the migration guide.
communication_plan:
- Public blog post and changelog at launch.
- In-product banner for org admins with counts of JSON-RPC calls in last 30 days.
- Targeted emails to org owners for top 200 orgs observed using JSON-RPC.
- Office hours webinar and migration office-hours recordings posted to docs.
- GitHub issue templates and SDK migration examples in example repos.
risk_mitigation:
- Keep automatic redirects enabled for 90 days to reduce forced downtime.
- Provide an opt-in migration CLI and dry-run to catch edge cases.
- Maintain a human-in-the-loop rollback path: restore alias mappings for affected orgs within 4 hours.
- Coordinate with Sales/SE to grant Dedicated customers extended windows where needed.
open_questions: What is acceptable error-rate uplift during redirect (engineering preferred threshold is +5%)?
Do we need an explicit SAML/OAuth token reissue flow for SDKs that embed auth in JSON-RPC payload?
Should we offer a paid migration service for customers with >100M tokens/month?
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Scoped requirement with ENG. Decided to extend redirect window to 90 days after risk review (see scope_changes).
2026-03-01: SDK patches opened for python/js/go; first CI failures triaged to parameter mapping differences. ENG to fix mapping shim. ENG-81221 assigned.
2026-03-08: Security review kick-off; initial note: confirm Deprecation header does not leak internal routing. Sec review due 2026-03-18.
success_metrics:
1) JSON-RPC request volume reduced by >=80% within 120 days of soft deprecation.
2) 95% of top-50 customers migrated within 180 days.
3) No more than 2 rollbacks needed for production-impacting regressions.
4) Developer satisfaction improved: migration docs rated >=4/5 in post-migration survey.
notes: Trade-offs: longer redirect window increases operational overhead but reduces customer risk. Decision taken to prioritize customer continuity over aggressive bit-rot removal. We will automate as much of the mapping as feasible but expect custom edge cases requiring SE engagement.
